clue.text: Layabout with this treatment making Waterloo flood?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer says put G (good) in place of O (nothing); doing that to WATERLOO gives WATERLOG, which means to flood

explanation.surface: A lazy idler is blamed for letting a London station get swamped.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: G (good) for O (nothing). Swap the last O of WATERLOO for G and you get WATERLOG, to flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is an idle, lazy person, which is exactly what a worthless good-for-nothing is.

clue.text: Hotel specialist tipped to run leaderless institution

indicators.note: to here simply joins on the next piece, which follows in sequence
tipped over, so hotel and specialist together are turned round

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pro is a professional, a specialist

indicators.note: without its leader, so the first letter of the word for run goes

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A hotel expert is expected to take charge of an institution that has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' reads as a noun qualifying specialist, but it is a separate letter from the NATO alphabet; 'tipped' and 'leaderless' are the two operations.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is a residential institution caring for children without parents.

clue.text: Centrist's head in the sand — one never learns

indicators.note: in means the head of the centrist is placed within the word for sand

parts.note: a dune is a ridge of sand

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Centrist's is used

explanation.surface: A political moderate burying their head in the sand is mocked as someone who never learns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C, the head of Centrist, inside DUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow pupil, someone who seems incapable of learning anything.

clue.text: What an expert knows related in special paper

parts.note: an expert is said to know their onions, a British idiom for being knowledgeable
kin means related by family, as in 'kin to'

explanation.surface: An expert's knowledge, it seems, is linked to some kind of special paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Know your onions' is a British idiom meaning to be expert in a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Onionskin is a very thin, translucent paper once used for carbon copies and airmail letters.

clue.text: Celebrated day with school over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the letters are turned upwards and read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A celebrated day as the school term finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns D plus ETON round, so DETON reads as the answer. Eton is an English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted is a synonym of famous or renowned, meaning widely known and celebrated.

clue.text: Expression silver worker used for brawling woman

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: A silversmith's phrase used to describe a quarrelsome woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a harsh, overbearing, quarrelsome woman; the name comes from an imaginary deity in medieval plays.

clue.text: Infantryman up to smallest room in White House?

indicators.note: to here means the soldier is followed by the room, joined on next in sequence
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, an infantryman
the smallest room is a jocular British name for the toilet, the loo

explanation.surface: A soldier heads up to the toilet at the US President's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' points to Washington, but the question mark signals a house that is literally white. 'Smallest room' is a British euphemism for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped house built of snow blocks, so it is literally white.

clue.text: Grand Hollywood star's fascinating beauty

parts.note: G is the slang abbreviation for a grand, a thousand
Dorothy Lamour was a Hollywood film star, famous for the Road movies with Bob Hope and Bing Crosby

explanation.surface: A grand Hollywood actress possesses captivating good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is alluring attractiveness, a beauty that captivates and fascinates.

clue.text: One wearing hose — Didi or Gogo?

indicators.note: wearing means the word for hose goes round the other piece like clothing

parts.note: to hose a garden is to water it
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone in stockings asks whether they are one of Beckett's two tramps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts I inside WATER. Didi and Gogo are the two tramps in Beckett's Waiting for Godot, who do nothing but wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Didi and Gogo spend the whole play waiting, so either is literally one who waits.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon author in Colorado resort

parts.note: to pen is to write, so pen stands for author in crosswords

explanation.surface: An Old English writer turns up at a Colorado ski resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspen is a well-known ski town in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado.

clue.text: Bury boxing champ meets American among others

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
Muhammad Ali was world heavyweight boxing champion

explanation.surface: A boxing champion is laid to rest alongside an American, among other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for 'among other things', used to introduce examples.

clue.text: Dinsdale's outside in coach for deal

indicators.note: in means the ends of the name are placed within the word for coach

parts.note: to coach someone is to train them

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone named Dinsdale waits outside a coach to strike a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes D and E, the ends of Dinsdale, and 'in' puts them into TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is a deal where an old item is handed over as part payment for a new one.

clue.text: Old boy back to fill face with duck and game

indicators.note: to fill means this piece goes inside the word for face

parts.note: a dial is a clock face, and also slang for a person's face

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so it looks like O

explanation.surface: An old boy returns to stuff his face with duck and game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' seems to continue the food theme, but it is the definition. A duck is a cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game in which a spool is spun and tossed on a string between two sticks.

clue.text: Arrive at stretch of river

definitions.meaning: to ... a place is to arrive at it
a straight stretch of river between bends

explanation.surface: Getting to a particular section of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Reach means to get to a destination, and is also a continuous straight length of water on a river.

clue.text: Messenger endlessly tough drinker in bouts?

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for tough is dropped

parts.note: hard means tough
a binger drinks heavily in bouts, binges

explanation.surface: A messenger is portrayed as a relentlessly hard man who drinks in sprees.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is a herald or forerunner, one who announces what is coming.

clue.text: Head going after goat snatcher

indicators.note: going after means the word for head comes after the word for goat

parts.note: a kid is a young goat
napper is old slang for the head

explanation.surface: A head chasing a goat thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper seizes and carries off a person, a snatcher of people.

clue.text: Don Corleone to start with poem in black tie?

parts.note: to don clothes is to dress in them

indicators.note: to start with means only the initial letter of Corleone is used

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: The Godfather Don Corleone begins with a poem at a formal evening event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like the Mafia title for Corleone but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Black tie' on an invitation is an example of a dress code, a rule about what to wear.

clue.text: Bird in spot having lost tail in plant

indicators.note: in means the bird sits within the shortened word for spot
having lost tail means the last letter of the word for spot is removed

parts.note: a spot is a pimple
the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A bird on a spot, having lost its tail, sits among the plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' invites a whole avian answer, but the bird is only the filling; 'plant' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small wild flower of the primrose family.

clue.text: About to find out about a church blessing

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: about here means around, so the word for find out goes round the a

parts.note: to learn is to find out
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Discovering a church's attitude to a blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside LEARN to give LEARAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is official permission or approval, a blessing in the sense of consent.

clue.text: Converse about Brazilian city's ancient two-wheeler

indicators.note: about means the word for converse goes around the city

parts.note: to converse is to chat
Rio de Janeiro is the Brazilian city

explanation.surface: Talking about a Brazilian city's old-fashioned bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converse' looks like the trainer brand or an adjective, but it is the verb to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot was a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used in ancient warfare and racing.

clue.text: Measure essential to stop me talking back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
something essential to these words is within them, so the letters are found inside

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A measure considered vital to keep someone from chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Measure essential' as the definition, but 'essential to' is the indicator for the hidden letters OPMET; 'back' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed or rate of a piece of music, its measure of pace.

clue.text: Be too clever for Basil Brush?

definitions.meaning: Basil Brush is a fox puppet on British children's TV

explanation.surface: Can you outsmart the famous puppet fox?
explanation.walkthrough: Basil Brush is a wisecracking fox glove puppet from British television since the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfox means to outwit or outmanoeuvre by cunning, as a fox is proverbially sly.

clue.text: Assign a parking place

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a point is a place or spot

explanation.surface: Allocating someone a parking space.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to assign a person to a job or role.

clue.text: Sweet nut — aquatic bird dropping large one

indicators.note: dropping means these letters are taken out of the bird's name

parts.note: a pelican is a large water bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sweet nut is let fall by a water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a sweet-tasting nut from a hickory tree, used in pies and pralines.

clue.text: Behind two others, what sort of man was Philby?

definitions.meaning: coming behind two others puts you ... in line

definitions.text: what sort of man was Philby?
definitions.meaning: Kim Philby, the Soviet spy, was known as the ... Man of the Cambridge spy ring

explanation.surface: Following two others, one wonders what kind of man the spy Philby was.
explanation.walkthrough: Philby was dubbed the 'Third Man' after Burgess and Maclean fled to Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: Third is the position after first and second, and the label attached to Philby in the spy scandal.

clue.text: Conspicuous way to involve stranger

indicators.note: to involve means to take in, so the way surrounds the stranger

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an alien is a stranger or foreigner

explanation.surface: An eye-catching method of getting a stranger involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is the street abbreviation, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or most noticeable, standing out as conspicuous.

clue.text: Drinks excessively from the outset, finding decline

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks

indicators.note: from the outset means only the opening letter of excessively is used

explanation.surface: Someone drinking to excess from the start is found to be on the slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a decline or falling off, a slip from a standard.

clue.text: Noticing anagrams with nothing disguised

indicators.note: with means the letter for nothing accompanies the rearranged letters, added on at the end
the clue openly says the word noticing is to be rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone spots anagrams with nothing hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagrams' rearranges NOTICING; O is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Incognito means with one's identity concealed, travelling disguised.

clue.text: Punter initially enthusiastic about horse

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of punter is taken

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: A gambler is at first excited about a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a horse with patchy markings of white and another colour.

clue.text: Time Dicky Small occupied with game in town

indicators.note: occupied with means the card game goes inside the other letters

parts.note: dicky is British slang for poorly or unwell
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Feeling poorly at one point, a small person kept busy with a game in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupied with' puts BRIDGE inside UNWELLS. Tunbridge Wells is a spa town in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Tunbridge Wells is a town in Kent, a stereotype of genteel English provincial life.
